A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QEP research work. All 28 pages of v2 and 29 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, runtime, calibration sensitivity, and repeated-seed experiments on quantized language models.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain these original empirical results and add FP16 reference results and an OmniQuant comparison.

M1.justification: The asymmetric reconstruction objective, weight correction, propagation-strength parameter, and integration with existing quantizers in Equations (3)–(6) remain unchanged. Revised mathematical derivations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain C4/Pile calibration, WikiText-2/PTB/C4 perplexity evaluation, and ARC-Easy/PIQA/StoryCloze zero-shot tasks. The added OmniQuant comparison uses an existing model and dataset; the newly discussed 1-bit approaches are not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds FP16 references to Tables 1–2 and evaluates OmniQuant in new Table 11. RTN, GPTQ, AWQ, and QuIP remain. GPTAQ and Defensive Quantization are newly discussed but are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve calibration sampling, including 128 C4 segments of 2,048 tokens, model configurations, bit/group settings, metrics, and propagation-strength defaults. Table 11 uses the existing Llama-2-7B/WikiText-2 precision grid without describing a distinct new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The partial-quantization analysis in Figure 2, calibration sensitivity comparison in Table 4, and seed-stability analysis accompanying Figure 3 are retained. Table 11 adds a benchmark comparison rather than an ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent QuIP runs, means and standard errors in Figure 3, and best-seed selection for main-text results. Appendix C.3 becomes D.3 without changing these practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add FP16 results. Table 11 newly reports OmniQuant perplexities of 5.880, 7.065, and NaN at INT4, INT3, and INT2; its QEP rows reproduce existing results. All previously reported table values and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces v2's Appendix A with formalized perturbation expansions, an exact error bound, a derivative-based first-order bound, and a scalar growth example replacing the general exponential lower-bound claim. Theorem B.5 changes actual-error dominance to upper-bound dominance; Corollary B.6 replaces global monotonicity with a fixed-layer bound. Ridge formulas are corrected and old Lemma A.8 is removed. However, Lemma B.8 changes the projection expansion coefficient from alpha(2-alpha) to the incorrect 2alpha(1-alpha).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and principal conclusion retain the same error-accumulation motivation, general lightweight QEP contribution, and emphasis on low-bit improvements. The broader guarantees stated in Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.4 also remain unchanged despite the appendix revisions.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds substantive discussion of difficulties near 1-bit precision and possible combinations with binary-factor and sparsity methods. The new Limitations paragraph extends the overfitting comparison to AWQ, while largely restating existing calibration-quality and propagation-parameter caveats.

D1.justification: v3 adds a QEP code-repository URL on the title page. The calibration recipe, single-V100 hardware disclosure, propagation-strength defaults, and Hessian damping instructions remain unchanged, including material moved from Appendix B.1 to C.1.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands research positioning: it compares QEP with Defensive Quantization, acknowledges GPTAQ's shared local objective, and argues differences in integration, guarantees, and propagation control. It also connects QEP to extreme low-bit parameterizations, binary factorization, and relaxation-based optimization through newly cited work.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the theoretical exposition are rewritten, replacing earlier induction-based narratives with separate exact, first-order, and fixed-layer analyses. A new related-work appendix and concluding Limitations paragraph reorganize the document. Main Sections 1–7 otherwise receive mostly limited copyediting and header/affiliation updates.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain FP16 rows, Table 11 is added, and Figure 3 moves alongside the supplementary experimental discussion. Citation links become colored. Existing plots and the overall table and page designs remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: FP16 references, the OmniQuant comparison, code-access information, and explicit positioning against GPTAQ make the paper easier to assess. Several derivations improve, notably replacing the unsupported general exponential lower bound with a valid scalar example. These are partial repairs: Theorem B.5 still uses an invalid residual-comparison step, the main global guarantees remain unreconciled with the revised appendix, and Lemma B.8 introduces an algebraic error.
